title: Photoluminescence measurements of carbon quantum dots within three-dimensional hydrogel matrices using a high throughput 96 well plate method
author: Truskewycz, Beker, et al.

steps.title: Synthesize QCDs and hydrogel
steps.instruction: Prepare fluorescent carbon quantum dots (QCDs) and a transparent hydrogel according to your established laboratory procedures.

steps.title: Blend QCDs with hydrogel
steps.instruction: Combine the synthesized QCDs with the transparent hydrogel to form a homogeneous hydrogel‑QCD composite.

steps.title: Dispense composite into plate
steps.instruction: Add 100 mg of the hydrogel‑QCD composite to each well of a black 96‑well plate; perform each condition in triplicate.

steps.title: Add test anions/cations
steps.instruction: Add 5 mM solutions of the desired anions/cations (including Cr⁶⁺, Fe²⁺, and other ions) to the appropriate wells; keep water‑only wells as controls.

steps.title: Prepare Cr6+ dilution series
steps.instruction: Create serial dilutions of hexavalent chromium (Cr⁶⁺) covering concentrations from 5.0 mM down to 0.234 mM (including the sub‑ranges 0.234–1.875 mM and 1.875–5.0 mM). Add each dilution to wells containing the hydrogel‑QCD composite.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Using a plate reader, record the photoluminescence (fluorescence) of each well; calculate relative fluorescence (F/F₀) where F₀ is the fluorescence of the water control.

steps.title: Analyze Stern‑Volmer data
steps.instruction: Plot (F₀/F − 1) versus Cr⁶⁺ concentration to generate Stern‑Volmer curves; identify the linear quenching range (0.234–1.875 mM) with R² = 0.9979 and note the deviation at 1.875–5.0 mM indicating multilayer adsorption; report the detection limit as 0.234 mM.

steps.title: Validate platform performance
steps.instruction: Confirm low variation among triplicate wells and repeatable fluorescence measurements to verify the sensing platform’s accuracy and reliability.
